topic: Ship It Right 02/04: Google doesn't know your app

cover.headline: Google Doesn’t Know Your App
cover.subtitle: Help search engines understand and display your pages.

slides.title: Meta Titles & Descriptions
slides.tip: Write a unique, relevant title and description for each important page. Treat character counts as guidelines, not display guarantees.
slides.quote: A clear page title and description help people understand what your page offers in search results.

slides.title: Social Preview Image
slides.tip: Add appropriate Open Graph metadata and use a clear, well-cropped preview image. A common starting point is 1200 × 630 pixels.
slides.quote: When someone shares your link, make the preview explain what the page is about.

slides.title: Favicon
slides.tip: Provide a legible icon at small sizes and test it against both light and dark browser UI.
slides.quote: A small, recognizable favicon makes your site easier to identify in browser tabs and bookmarks.

slides.title: Sitemap & robots.txt
slides.tip: Include canonical, indexable pages in your sitemap. Don’t use robots.txt as a way to protect private content.
slides.quote: A sitemap helps search engines discover important URLs; robots.txt tells crawlers which paths they may request.

slides.title: Image Alt Text
slides.tip: Write concise, contextual descriptions. Use empty alt text for purely decorative images instead of stuffing keywords.
slides.quote: Useful alt text describes an image’s purpose for people who can’t see it.

slides.title: Structured Data
slides.tip: Add valid schema markup only when it accurately describes the page, then test it with the relevant search tools.
slides.quote: Structured data can help search engines interpret eligible content, but it doesn’t guarantee a rich result.

slides.title: Open Graph & Social Tags
slides.tip: Set Open Graph tags and, where supported, platform-specific card metadata. Keep previews consistent with the actual page.
slides.quote: Control how your page appears when shared by defining its title, description, image, and relevant platform metadata.

slides.title: Test on Social Platforms
slides.tip: Test important URLs on the platforms your audience uses, including messaging apps, and check image cropping and text.
slides.quote: A preview that looks right on your site can still look broken when shared elsewhere.

slides.title: What’s your site missing?
slides.description: Check your homepage. Pick the weak spot.

caption.caption:
Google doesn’t know your app until you tell it. Titles, previews, favicons, sitemaps, alt text and structured data, checked before launch.

None of these guarantee rankings or rich results; they help search engines and people understand your pages.
caption.cta: Comment one: Title, Preview or Favicon
